mainTopic: The נזיר's foreleg as a חידוש for nullifying the flavor of קדשים, and אביי's challenge to the one-hundred rule from the משנה of split beans and lentils
overview: The amud begins with the cooked foreleg (זרוע בשלה) of the נזיר's ram, which is קדשים, yet its flavor does not forbid the rest of the ram. The גמרא asks whether we can learn from this that the flavor of קדשים is always nullified. It answers no: the פסוק about חטאת teaches that food absorbing its flavor takes on its status. The נזיר case is a חידוש, and we do not learn general rules from a חידוש. We still learn the 100 or 60 measure from it, because that is only a stringency: by Torah law a simple majority would be enough. רבינא gives another reading of the case: it comes to permit the place of the cut (מקום חתך). Then רב דימי repeats the rule that forbidden food is nullified only in one hundred. אביי challenges him from a משנה about תרומה split beans cooked with lentils, where taste alone decides, and argues that the amount that works there must be sixty, not one hundred.

steps.title: Let us learn from the נזיר's foreleg
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests learning from the זרוע בשלה that the flavor of קדשים is nullified in general.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges: since the foreleg's flavor did not forbid the rest of the ram, maybe the flavor of קדשים never forbids other food. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The foreleg is holy food (קדשים) cooked with the rest of the ram, which is eaten under different rules, and its flavor does not affect the rest. So it looks like a model case showing that the flavor of קדשים can be nullified everywhere.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn (a general rule) from it
The cooked foreleg given to the כהן from the נזיר's ram

phrases.english: And let us learn from it?
phrases.notes: "It" means the case of the נזיר's ram, whose foreleg's flavor did not forbid the rest of the meat.

steps.kashyaTarget: The idea that the flavor of קדשים is never nullified
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The זרוע בשלה shows flavor of קדשים being nullified, so make it a general rule.

steps.title: The Torah revealed about חטאת that absorbed flavor takes on its status
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק about חטאת teaches that food absorbing its flavor becomes like it, so the flavor of קדשים is not nullified.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Torah revealed regarding a חטאת: 'Whatever touches its flesh shall become holy.' This means it becomes like the חטאת: if the חטאת is disqualified, the food is disqualified too, and if the חטאת is valid, the food is eaten under the strict rules of the חטאת.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that we cannot make a general rule from the foreleg. A פסוק about חטאת shows the opposite: food that absorbs flavor from קדשים takes on its holy status.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'shall become holy' mean the food that absorbed the flavor becomes just like the חטאת, with all its rules and limits. So the flavor of קדשים is clearly not nullified, and the Torah itself shows this.

keyTerms.meaning: The Merciful One (the Torah) revealed
Sin offering
To be like it (to take on its status)
According to its strictest rules

phrases.english: The Merciful One revealed regarding a sin offering:
"Whatever shall touch its flesh shall become holy,"
to be like it –
that if it is disqualified, this too shall be disqualified,
and if it is valid, it is eaten according to its strictest rules.

steps.terutzResolutionType: A competing פסוק shows the opposite rule
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learn from the זרוע that the flavor of קדשים is nullified
steps.terutzMaskana: The חטאת פסוק teaches that absorbed flavor takes on the status of the קדשים

steps.title: Why learn from חטאת rather than from the נזיר?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why we choose the חטאת source over the נזיר source.
steps.simpleTranslation: What makes you learn from that one (חטאת)? Learn from this one (the נזיר's ram)!
steps.whatsHappening: There are two sources that point in opposite directions. The גמרא asks why we follow חטאת instead of the נזיר.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both are cases written in the Torah. Without a reason to prefer one, the choice of חטאת looks arbitrary.

keyTerms.meaning: What did you see? (Why choose this over that?)
That one / this one

phrases.english: And what did you see that we learn from that one,
phrases.notes: "That one" is the חטאת. "This one" in the next line is the נזיר's ram.

phrases.english: let us learn from this one?

steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Two opposite sources exist, so there is no reason to prefer חטאת.

steps.title: The נזיר's foreleg is a חידוש
steps.stepSummary: The זרוע of the נזיר is a one-time exception, and we do not learn general rules from exceptions.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a novelty, and we do not learn from a novelty.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the נזיר case is a special exception, so it cannot be used to make a general rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חידוש goes against the normal logic of the Torah. The Torah allowed it only in that one place. So the general rule comes from חטאת, and the נזיר case stays a single exception.

keyTerms.meaning: A novelty, an exception to normal rules
We do not learn from a novelty

steps.whatToRemember: The נזיר's foreleg is a חידוש. The general rule is that the flavor of קדשים is not nullified (learned from חטאת).
steps.confusionAlert: The foreleg is still truly קדשים. The חידוש is only in how its flavor is treated, not in whether it is holy.

phrases.english: It is a novelty,
and from a novelty we do not learn.

steps.terutzResolutionType: The case is set aside as a חידוש
steps.terutzMaskana: The נזיר case is an exception and cannot teach a general rule

steps.title: Then don't learn 100 or 60 from it either
steps.stepSummary: If we don't learn from a חידוש, how do we learn the amounts of 100 or 60 for nullification from the נזיר's ram?
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, we should also not learn the rule of one hundred or sixty from it!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back. We do use the נזיר's ram as the source for nullifying forbidden food in 100 or 60 times its amount, so how can we call it a case we cannot learn from?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier, the opinions requiring 100 or 60 were both based on the size of the foreleg compared to the rest of the ram. Calling the case a חידוש seems to knock out that source too.

keyTerms.meaning: If so
One hundred or sixty: the two opinions on how much is needed to nullify forbidden flavor (not the number 160)

phrases.english: If so,
for one hundred or sixty, too, we should not learn?
phrases.notes: This is the rule that forbidden food is cancelled out in 100 times (or 60 times) its amount, a rule learned from this ram.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי הָכִי לְמֵאָה וְשִׁשִּׁים נָמֵי לָא לִיגְמַר
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim in step 4 that we do not learn from the נזיר case
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: We already learn the 100 or 60 rule from this same case.

steps.title: We learn only a stringency from it
steps.stepSummary: The 100 or 60 rule is a stringency, since by Torah law a simple majority would nullify.
steps.simpleTranslation: Do you think we learn a leniency from it? We learn a stringency, because by Torah law forbidden food is nullified in a majority.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that learning 100 or 60 is not a leniency. It makes things stricter than the basic Torah rule of רוב (majority).
steps.deeperAnalysis: We do not learn leniencies from a חידוש. But here, without this source we would say a simple majority is enough. So the 100 or 60 rule only adds strictness, and learning that from the case is fine.

keyTerms.meaning: Do you think? (introduces a rejected assumption)
As a leniency / as a stringency
By Torah law
It is nullified in a majority

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows the basic idea that by Torah law forbidden food is nullified in a simple majority. The larger amounts are an added stringency.

phrases.english: Is it that we learn it as a leniency?
We learn it as a stringency,
since by Torah law it is nullified in a majority.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: Learning 100 or 60 would mean learning from a חידוש
steps.terutzMaskana: Only a stringency is learned, and a stringency can be learned even from a חידוש

steps.title: רבינא: the ברייתא comes to permit the place of the cut
steps.stepSummary: רבינא explains that the ברייתא's lesson is that the place where the foreleg was cut off stays permitted here.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: It is needed only for the place of the cut. Normally, the place of the cut is forbidden, but here it is permitted.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא gives a different explanation of what the ברייתא about the נזיר's foreleg is teaching. It is about the spot where the foreleg was cut from the ram.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Normally, when a forbidden piece is attached to a permitted piece and is cut off, the cut spot on the permitted piece stays forbidden. With the נזיר's ram, the cut spot on the rest of the ram is permitted. That is the חידוש according to רבינא.

keyTerms.meaning: It was needed only for
The place of the cut
Generally, in other cases
Permitted

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבינא, the חידוש of the נזיר's foreleg is that the place of the cut is permitted, unlike in other cases.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
It was needed only for the place of the cut,
phrases.notes: The ברייתא's words "this is" about the foreleg teach only about the spot where it was cut off the ram.

phrases.english: for it was said: the place of the cut is generally forbidden,
but here it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: רָבִינָא אָמַר לֹא נִצְרְכָה אֶלָּא לִמְקוֹם חֲתָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a different reading of the ברייתא from the one discussed in steps 1–6
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In the case of the נזיר's ram, the place where the foreleg was cut off is permitted, unlike the general rule.

steps.title: רב דימי repeats the one-hundred teaching
steps.stepSummary: רב דימי sits and teaches the earlier statement that forbidden food is nullified only in one hundred times its volume.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב דימי sat and said this teaching.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to the earlier rule about nullifying forbidden food in one hundred. It shows רב דימי teaching it. This line sets up אביי's challenge in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Nothing new is argued here. The point is to bring the one-hundred rule back into focus, so that אביי can question how broadly it applies.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching or legal statement
Sat, meaning he was sitting and teaching

phrases.english: Rav Dimi sat
and was saying this teaching.
phrases.notes: "This teaching" is the earlier statement that forbidden food is nullified only in one hundred times its volume.

steps.triggerLanguage: יָתֵיב רַב דִּימִי וְקָאָמַר לַהּ לְהָא שְׁמַעְתָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves רבינא's point about the foreleg and returns to the general one-hundred nullification rule.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Forbidden food mixed with permitted food is nullified only in one hundred times its volume.

steps.title: אביי questions whether every prohibition needs one hundred
steps.stepSummary: אביי asks whether all Torah prohibitions really need one hundred. He quotes a משנה that treats same-type and different-type mixtures of תרומה differently.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said to him: Are all the prohibitions in the Torah nullified only in one hundred? But we learned in a משנה: Why did they say that whoever leavens, flavors, or mixes תרומה into regular food is treated strictly when it is the same type, but both leniently and strictly when it is a different type?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי challenges רב דימי by asking whether the one-hundred rule really covers every prohibition. He starts quoting a משנה about תרומה mixtures to prove his point.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה divides mixtures into two kinds. With the same type of food we are only stringent. With a different type we are sometimes lenient and sometimes stringent. That second category hints that a different measure, not one hundred, is in play. The next step makes this explicit.

keyTerms.meaning: One who leavens dough with a forbidden leavening agent
One who flavors food with forbidden spices
One who mixes תְּרוּמָה into regular food, making it forbidden to non-כֹּהֲנִים
A mixture of the same type of food
A mixture of different types of food

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
And are all the prohibitions in the Torah nullified in one hundred?
But didn't we learn in a mishna:
Why did they say
that anyone who leavens, or flavors, or mixes in terumah
is treated stringently when it is one type with its own type,
but both leniently and stringently when it is one type with a different type.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly attacks the rule רב דימי just taught.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that every Torah prohibition is nullified only in one hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A משנה gives a separate treatment, both lenient and strict, to mixtures of different types. That suggests a measure other than one hundred decides those cases.

steps.title: Split beans and lentils: taste decides, not one hundred
steps.stepSummary: The later part of the משנה explains: תרומה split beans cooked with lentils are forbidden if they give taste and permitted if they don't, no matter whether there is 101.
steps.simpleTranslation: The later part teaches: How are we lenient and strict with different types? Split beans of תרומה were cooked with lentils. If the beans give taste, the mixture is forbidden, whether or not there is enough to nullify them in 101. If they do not give taste, it is permitted, whether or not there is enough to nullify them in 101.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי continues his challenge by quoting the rest of the משנה. It shows that when the foods are of different types, only taste matters. The next step draws the conclusion that makes this a real problem.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "Stringent" means that even with more than 101, the mixture is forbidden if the תרומה's taste is noticeable. "Lenient" means that even with less than 101, it is permitted if there is no taste. So for different types the count of one hundred is not what decides. אביי will use the lenient case to show that a smaller amount, sixty, must be enough.

keyTerms.meaning: The later part of a משנה or ברייתא
Split beans
Lentils
Gives taste, meaning the forbidden food's flavor can be noticed in the mixture
To nullify in 101, the standard measure for תְּרוּמָה

steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the 101 count has some role here. For different types the משנה says the count makes no difference in either direction. Only taste decides.
steps.whatToRemember: With a different type of food, the test is taste (נותן טעם), not one hundred. That is the basis for אביי's challenge to the claim that every prohibition needs one hundred.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the next stage, where the גמרא must limit the one-hundred rule or explain where it applies.

phrases.english: And it teaches in the later part:

phrases.aramaic: לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר מִין וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ, כֵּיצַד?
phrases.english: Leniently and stringently with one type and a different type, how so?
Split beans that were cooked with lentils:
phrases.notes: The split beans are תרומה and the lentils are regular food.

phrases.english: if they are enough to give taste,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין יֵשׁ בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: whether there is enough to nullify them in one hundred and one,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אֵין בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – אָסוּר.
phrases.english: or there is not enough to nullify them in one hundred and one, it is forbidden.
If they are not enough to give taste,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁיֵּשׁ בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד,
phrases.english: whether there is enough to nullify them in one hundred and one,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין אֵין בָּהֶן לְהַעֲלוֹת בְּמֵאָה וְאֶחָד – מוּתָּר.
phrases.english: or there is not enough to nullify them in one hundred and one, it is permitted.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְקָתָנֵי סֵיפָא לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחְמִיר מִין וְשֶׁאֵינוֹ מִינוֹ כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes אביי's challenge by quoting the case that defines "lenient and stringent" for different types.
steps.raayaObject: That not all prohibitions are measured by one hundred.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The משנה in ערלה about split beans of תרומה cooked with lentils, where taste alone decides.

steps.title: If not in 101, then it must be in sixty
steps.stepSummary: אביי reads the משנה closely: if the beans are permitted even without 101, the amount that works must be sixty. That goes against the rule of one hundred.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says there is not enough to cancel it out in 101. So in what amount is it cancelled? Isn't it in sixty?
steps.whatsHappening: אביי finishes his question by squeezing an inference out of the משנה's words. He shows that the משנה points to sixty, not one hundred.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה says the beans are permitted if they give no taste, even when there is not 101 times as much. So some smaller amount must already be enough to cancel them. אביי says that amount is sixty, which goes against the claim that all forbidden food needs one hundred.

keyTerms.meaning: to cancel out the forbidden food (literally 'to lift it up'), so the mixture becomes permitted
101: the amount the משנה needs to cancel תרומה mixed with the same kind of food
sixty times as much: the amount at which a taste no longer comes through
'isn't it…?': a question that expects the answer 'yes'

steps.confusionAlert: 'Isn't it in sixty?' is not a real open question. אביי is pushing his point: the answer has to be sixty, and that is the problem for the one-hundred rule.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the clash between 'one hundred' and 'sixty' that the גמרא must now settle.

phrases.english: There is not enough in them to cancel it out in one hundred and one,
phrases.notes: אביי is quoting the משנה's own words: there are not enough lentils for the mixture to reach 101 parts in all for each part of תרומה beans.

phrases.english: so in what amount is it cancelled?
Is it not in sixty?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws the conclusion from the part of the משנה quoted in step 10 and finishes אביי's challenge from step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The statement רב דימי taught (step 8), that forbidden food is nullified only in one hundred.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The משנה permits the beans without 101 if they give no taste. So a smaller amount, sixty, must be enough. That goes against needing one hundred.
